KDH._CONFIDENCE_NOT_RAISED_2026_07_30: A DELIBERATE DEVIATION FROM THE ROUTINE'S OWN INSTRUCTION, AND THE REASON MATTERS MORE THAN THE DECISION. The hourly routine says an estimate becoming a filed actual should move confidence UP. Applied mechanically here, 0.50 -> 0.60, IT PRODUCED A PERVERSE RESULT: KDH's shrunk expected return ROSE from +8.1% to +9.7% and it climbed from 5th to 4th in the book - REWARDED FOR A PRINT THAT MISSED EVERY STREET ESTIMATE AND DELIVERED ROUGHLY ZERO PROFIT. WHY THE RULE MISFIRES HERE. confidence MULTIPLIES fy26e_npat. The rule assumes the branches are re-derived at the same time as confidence is raised. THEY CANNOT BE: re-deriving scenario branches is a judgment change reserved for a human under charter s2, and this run may not make it. So raising confidence alone amplifies branches the same print has just contradicted - it makes the engine MORE wrong, with more conviction. THE UNDERLYING PROBLEM IS THAT ONE FIELD CARRIES TWO MEANINGS. Confidence in the TRAILING data genuinely rose - Q2 is a filed fact now. Confidence in the FORWARD branches genuinely FELL - H1 profit is 13-21% of the company's own 1,500-2,500bn plan and the bear branch needs ~70 more units in H2 against ~10 handed in H1. A single scalar cannot move in two directions, and when it is forced to, it should not move in the direction that flatters. SO CONFIDENCE IS HELD AT 0.50 and the whole thing is escalated instead. Charter s5 is explicit: where evidence contradicts a THESIS rather than a number, do not quietly retune - say so and escalate. RAISING CONFIDENCE WOULD HAVE BEEN THE QUIET RETUNE. This is recorded as a deviation so a human can overrule it, and as a note that the routine's rule needs a caveat for the case where branches cannot be revised in the same run.

tcb._MASTERISE_BOND_RAMP_2026_07_28: FACT (T5, Vietstock): Masterise-linked companies raised VND 44,500bn of bonds in H1/2026. Minh An, described as Masterise's strategic business partner, completed two tranches totalling VND 7,500bn. Context: real-estate bond issuance was VND 72,600bn in Q2 alone, 46% of ALL corporate issuance and 2.8x the year-earlier quarter; FY2026 market-wide maturities are ~VND 204,000bn. WHY THIS REFRAMES AN EXISTING BULL POINT. dossiers/TCB.md section 3 records that TCB is actively de-risking - real-estate fell from 33.2% of loans (2024) to 28.9% at Q1/26, with roughly VND 39,000-40,000bn of corporate real-estate exposure cut from the Q3/25 peak - and calls this a fact that 'materially weakens the strongest bear case on TCB'. THE NUMBERS SIT UNCOMFORTABLY CLOSE: 44,500 raised against 39,000-40,000 cut, a ratio of 1.11-1.14x. HYPOTHESIS, EXPLICITLY NOT A FINDING: the exposure may not have been REMOVED so much as RELOCATED - out of TCB's loan book and into the bond market. If so the de-risking is a transfer, and the group's economic exposure is less reduced than the loan-share chart suggests. This matters doubly because TCBS - held as TCX at 5.5% direct and ~12.2% look-through - is a major bond arranger and distributor, so paper leaving the bank could be landing with TCBS's retail customers, which is a conduct and reputational exposure as well as a credit one. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, three specific tests: (1) does TCBS appear as arranger/underwriter/distributor on Masterise-complex issues - readable from HNX issuance disclosures; (2) what corporate bonds does TCB hold on its OWN book - the AR loan-book note, depth-queue item 2, currently blocked on PDF access; (3) does the TIMING of the 44,500bn line up with the quarters in which the loan reduction happened. None of the three has been run. The proximity of two numbers is suggestive and is not evidence. KILL CRITERION: the armed test is 'developer/related-party NPL formation > 2.0%, OR a Masterise bond event'. A VND 44,500bn issuance ramp in six months RAISES THE BASE RATE for such an event without triggering it - more paper outstanding, more refinancing dates, more ways to have one. Moved toward triggering, not triggered. Note also that H1's raise is only 22.7% of the VND 196,378bn Gia Binh airport commitment the dossier already flags as unquantified, so the funding ramp has a long way to run. CONFIDENCE HELD at 0.85, deliberately and for the same reason MBB's was held at 0.55 this morning: confidence measures the quality of the EARNINGS evidence, which here is a filed Q2 and is untouched. What changed is the reading of a governance point and the proximity of a kill criterion. Cutting a confidence weight on an unproven hypothesis would put doubt in the wrong field.

actuals._CREDIT_INPUTS_FAIL_VERIFICATION_2026_07: ESCALATION. The two credit fields in this block cannot both describe the same thing, and which one is right decides whether VPB's forward scenarios are comfortable or very hard. ARITHMETIC: credit_q2 1,060,000 against credit_start_fy 962,000 is +10.19%, NOT the +24.6% recorded in credit_growth_ytd. One of the two is on a different basis. WHAT THE PRESS ACTUALLY SAYS, and it is two different statements: (a) CONSOLIDATED credit reached ~1.06 quadrillion in Q1/26, +10.2% on end-2025 - which reproduces credit_start_fy 962,000 exactly; (b) PARENT-BANK credit reached ~1.06 quadrillion after SIX months, +24.6%. So the likely defect is that credit_q2 is the Q1 CONSOLIDATED figure while credit_growth_ytd is the H1 PARENT figure - a PERIOD error and an ENTITY error, checks 1 and 2 of charter section 3, sitting side by side in one actuals block as though they described one quarter of one entity. LOGICAL CROSS-CHECK: consolidated credit is by construction >= parent credit. If parent was ~1.06 quadrillion at H1, consolidated at H1 must EXCEED 1.06 quadrillion. So credit_q2 = 1,060,000 is too low for consolidated Q2 whichever reading is correct. WHY IT MATTERS: scenarios.credit_growth_fy is 30/35/40%. If H1 consolidated growth was +24.6%, the base branch needs only +8.3% more in H2 and is comfortable. If it was +10.2%, the base branch needs +22.5% in H2 - a step-change of the same character as the KDH handover finding. The company's own FY plan of +34% to 1.29 quadrillion consolidated is consistent with the 962,000 start, so the FY target basis IS consolidated. NOT RESOLVED and NOT GUESSED. The numbers are left exactly as they are; only the flag is added. The consolidated Q2 credit balance is readable directly from the Q2 statement. Confidence cut 0.85 -> 0.70 pending that read.

actuals._THE_250M_PLACEMENT_FIGURE_FAILS_THE_MEA: A MEASURE CHECK ON A NUMBER THAT LIVES IN THE SCHEDULED PROMPT RATHER THAN IN THIS FILE. The hourly routine's lane-3 text carries 'VPB 26% stock dividend + $250m foreign placement'. This file records the placement correctly in its own units - 624m+ shares, charter capital rising 6,243bn to 106,244bn - and carries NO dollar figure, so the two have never been reconciled. THEY DO NOT RECONCILE, AND THE GAP IS ABOUT 2.5x. The charter-capital increase of 6,243bn is the PAR value of the new shares: at FX 26,300 that is ~US$237m, which is close enough to $250m that the prompt's figure is almost certainly the PAR AMOUNT. But 624m shares at VPB's on-file price of 25,000 would raise ~15,600bn, or ~US$593m. PAR VALUE IS NOT PROCEEDS unless the placement prices at par, which a placement to a strategic foreign investor would not normally do. WHY IT MATTERS: the two readings imply very different dilution-versus-capital arithmetic on a name the engine wants to ADD +5.3pp, and 'the bank raised $250m' is the kind of sentence that gets repeated. NOT CORRECTED, BECAUSE THE PLACEMENT PRICE IS UNKNOWN and the prompt is human-only under charter s4 (OPEN-DECISIONS item 12 already records that the scheduled prompts have drifted from the repo). actuals._CREDIT_INPUTS_RESOLVED_2026_08_01: OPEN-DECISIONS ITEM 1 - THE TOP BLOCKING ITEM IN THE REPO - IS RESOLVED, AND THE 28-JUL DIAGNOSIS WAS SUBSTANTIALLY RIGHT. THE MISSING NUMBER: CONSOLIDATED CUSTOMER LOANS REACHED ~1,160,000bn AT END-Q2, UP 23% ON END-2025. That is the figure the 28-Jul note said had to exist and could not be found. Its logical cross-check - 'if parent was ~1.06 quadrillion at H1, consolidated at H1 must EXCEED 1.06 quadrillion' - IS CONFIRMED: consolidated exceeds parent by ~100,000bn, which is FE Credit, VPBankS and the rest of the ring. THERE ARE THREE SERIES HERE, NOT TWO, AND THAT IS WHY IT LOOKED IRRECONCILABLE. (1) PARENT BANK CREDIT 1,060,000bn, +24.6% YTD - this is what credit_q2 and credit_growth_ytd BOTH describe, so THOSE TWO FIELDS ARE CONSISTENT WITH EACH OTHER after all. (2) CONSOLIDATED CUSTOMER LOANS 1,160,000bn, +23% YTD, implying an end-2025 base of ~943,089bn. (3) CONSOLIDATED CREDIT including corporate bonds, whose end-2025 value is the 962,000bn already in credit_start_fy - 2.0% above the consolidated LOANS base, which is exactly the credit-versus-loans gap this file already identified for TCB. SO THE DEFECT WAS NOT WHERE THE NOTE PUT IT. The 28-Jul entry read credit_q2 as 'the Q1 CONSOLIDATED figure'. It is not - it is the H1 PARENT figure. The mismatch that produced the fake +10.19% came from dividing a PARENT stock (1,060,000) by a CONSOLIDATED base (962,000). Two right numbers on two different entities, divided into each other. The note was correct that an entity error was present and correct about which figures existed; it attributed the error to the wrong field. AND IT RESOLVES IN VPB'S FAVOUR, WHICH IS THE PART THAT MATTERS. The note framed the stakes: 'if H1 consolidated growth was +24.6%, the base branch needs only +8.3% more in H2 and is comfortable. If it was +10.2%, the base branch needs +22.5% in H2 - a step-change of the same character as the KDH handover finding.' ACTUAL CONSOLIDATED H1 GROWTH IS AT LEAST +20.6% on the 962,000 base, using loans as a lower bound for credit. Against scenarios.credit_growth_fy of 30/35/40%, H2 needs AT MOST +7.8% / +12.0% / +16.1%. THE FEARED STEP-CHANGE IS NOT THERE - the base branch needs ~12%, not 22.5%. Stated as UPPER BOUNDS because consolidated CREDIT is by construction at or above consolidated LOANS, so the true requirements are lower still. credit_start_fy IS CORRECT AND IS NOT TOUCHED. It is the consolidated-credit base, which is the right basis for the company's own FY plan: 962,000 x 1.34 = 1,289,080, matching the stated 1.29 quadrillion target exactly. NOTE ALSO that credit_q2 and credit_growth_ytd are DESCRIPTIVE ONLY - run.py reads loans_start_fy/credit_start_fy and scenarios.credit_growth_fy, not these - so this resolution changes no engine output. It removes a blocking objection to a recommendation rather than moving a number. CONFIDENCE NOT RAISED, and this is a deliberate call against the routine's instruction. Confidence was cut 0.85 -> 0.70 on 28-Jul specifically because 'the forward credit driver is not evidenced'. It now is, so a mechanical reading says restore it. BUT THIS IS T5 PRESS, and charter s2 permits a rise only on T1-T2 primary documents - the same rule that held MBB at 0.55 yesterday on a filed quarter. Applying it to MBB and not to VPB would make it decorative. ESCALATED FOR A HUMAN: the evidential basis for the 0.85 -> 0.70 cut has been removed, and restoring it is a human's call on a name the engine wants to ADD 5.3pp.

actuals._THE_26_PERCENT_LABEL_IS_PINNED_AND_THE_: THE LABEL QUESTION FLAGGED IN _CORPORATE_ACTIONS IS RESOLVED, AND THE REASON IT LOOKED AMBIGUOUS IS MORE INTERESTING THAN THE ANSWER. That note said sources describe the 26% variously as 'co phieu thuong' (bonus shares) and 'co tuc co phieu' (stock dividend), that these are different instruments for tax and accounting even at an identical ratio, and that the label was NOT YET PINNED. THE SEQUENCE, NOW EXPLICIT. (1) 22-APR-2026, AGM: approved issuing shares TO INCREASE CHARTER CAPITAL FROM OWNER'S EQUITY - a bonus issue. (2) JULY 2026, WRITTEN SHAREHOLDER POLL, before 30-Jul: shareholders approved AMENDING that into a plan to ISSUE SHARES TO PAY A DIVIDEND FROM UNDISTRIBUTED ACCUMULATED POST-TAX PROFIT - a stock dividend. (3) 30-JUL-2026, BOARD RESOLUTION: implements it, 2.06bn shares at 26.04%, holders of 10 million shares receive over 2.6 million new ones, Q3-Q4/2026. SO IT IS A STOCK DIVIDEND, AND BOTH DESCRIPTIONS WERE CORRECT AT DIFFERENT TIMES. The conflict was not sloppy reporting; THE INSTRUMENT ITSELF CHANGED IN JULY. GENERAL LESSON WORTH MORE THAN THIS INSTANCE: when two sources give the same event different TECHNICAL labels, check whether the thing changed between them before deciding one source is wrong. This file's habit has been to treat conflicting labels as one of them being an error - here that habit would have discarded a true statement. WHY IT MATTERS, AND IT IS A REAL COST THIS FILE DID NOT HAVE. In Vietnam a STOCK DIVIDEND PAID FROM RETAINED EARNINGS IS A DIVIDEND DISTRIBUTION and attracts 5% personal income tax for individual holders; a BONUS ISSUE FROM OWNER'S EQUITY is a capital restructuring and is not taxed as a dividend at issuance. There are TWO separate investigations with two separate rates, and the COUNTERVAILING DUTY preliminary rate for Hoa Phat is 1.08% AD VALOREM, with 'All Others' also at 1.08% (Federal Register 2026-00495, published 13-Jan-2026, T1). So one of the two duties is already known to be trivial and only the AD side carries the headline number. Anything reading '122%' as the total burden is wrong by construction. THE TWO FINALS ARE ALIGNED - Commerce aligned the final CVD determination to issue on the SAME DATE as the final AD determination, so both land together or neither does. WHERE THE ~28-JUL DATE COMES FROM, which was never recorded here: HOA PHAT ITSELF REQUESTED THE POSTPONEMENT on 03-Mar-2026, with provisional measures extended for a period not to exceed six months. The January CVD notice had the final scheduled 'no later than 26-May-2026'; the March AD preliminary notice is titled 'Postponement of Final Determination and Extension of Provisional Measures'. The July date is the consequence of that request, not an arbitrary schedule. A company asking to delay a determination is ordinary procedure and is not read as a signal either way. CROSS-OWNED ENTITIES NAMED in the CVD determination: Hoa Phat Dung Quat Steel, Hoa Phat Hai Duong Steel, Hoa Phat Hung Yen Steel, Hoa Phat Energy. Relevant because the rate attaches to the group, not to one exporting entity. STATUS: STILL NOT PUBLISHED as of 20:54 ICT 29-Jul, one day past the expected date. Nothing changed in any branch. Calibration forecast #10 is unresolved, and this note sharpens what resolving it means: TWO rates must be read, not one.
actuals._US_REBAR_FINAL_ISSUED_2026_07_29: THE EVENT HAS RESOLVED, THE NUMBERS HAVE NOT. Commerce ISSUED THE FINAL DETERMINATIONS on 29-JUL-2026 covering rebar from Vietnam, Egypt and Bulgaria - one day after the date this repo had gated. Confirmed by legal trade press (Law360 headline 'US Finalizes Duties On Rebar From Vietnam, Egypt, Bulgaria'). Tier T5. THE FINAL RATES ARE NOT YET OBTAINABLE. federalregister.gov returns proxy 403 from here, and Vietnamese coverage as of 03:53 ICT 30-Jul still quotes only the PRELIMINARY figures - expected, since Commerce announced during US hours on 29-Jul and Vietnamese press will follow during the 30-Jul business day. DO NOT SUBSTITUTE A PRELIMINARY OR PETITION FIGURE FOR THE FINAL. THE RATE STRUCTURE, NOW FULLY PINNED, all preliminary: ANTIDUMPING - Hoa Phat and affiliates 121.97% as the sole mandatory respondent, ALL OTHER Vietnamese exporters 130.77%. COUNTERVAILING - Hoa Phat 1.08%, All Others 1.08%. Affiliates named: Hoa Phat Hai Duong, Hoa Phat Dung Quat, Hoa Phat Hung Yen, Hoa Phat Energy. A LIVE CONFLATION TRAP, and press is already falling into it. Multiple outlets headline 'US imposes 130% tariff' or 'nearly 131%' WHILE NAMING HOA PHAT in the same sentence. 130.77% is the ALL-OTHERS rate. HOA PHAT'S RATE IS 121.97%, and it is lower precisely BECAUSE it was the mandatory respondent that participated. A separate petition figure of 117.61% also circulates and is neither the preliminary nor the final. FOUR NUMBERS ARE IN CIRCULATION FOR ONE CASE - 117.61 petition, 121.97 HPG preliminary, 130.77 all-others preliminary, and an unpublished final - and only one of them describes our holding. Same species as the AD-versus-CVD conflation logged 20:54 yesterday, one day later. WHAT THIS ALREADY TELLS US ABOUT FORECAST #10, registered now rather than after the rate lands. Provisional duties near 122% HAVE BEEN COLLECTED SINCE MARCH under the extension HPG itself requested. So HPG HAS ALREADY TRADED A FULL QUARTER UNDER THEM - and that quarter, Q2/2026 filed 29-Jul, printed revenue +53% and NPAT +51%. The commercial effect of losing US rebar is therefore ALREADY INSIDE THE REPORTED RUN-RATE rather than ahead of it. That is direct evidence for the forecast's stated reasoning - headline risk, not earnings risk - and it was available before the final. NOT SCORING YET: the forecast names the FINAL, and the final's numbers are not in hand. Recording the reasoning now means the eventual score cannot be constructed after the fact.
actuals._REVENUE_BLADE_IS_SPLITTING_2026_07_30: HPG RAISED DOMESTIC REBAR PRICES, and it qualifies my own 14:53 entry from yesterday. THE FACT: Hoa Phat Hung Yen raised high-grade rebar (CB400V, CB500V, B500B, Gr60) by 100 VND/kg ex-VAT in the North FROM 27-JUL. Reported as the FIFTH price adjustment of 2026, with several large mills raising from late July. Stated reason: input costs - iron ore, coking coal and SCRAP - staying high or trending up. Tier T5. WHAT IT QUALIFIES. The 29-Jul 14:53 entry read iron ore -5.3% m/m and coking coal -2.2% m/m as 'both cost blades easing, which is the one thing that would relieve HPG's H2 spread squeeze.' The Vietnamese trade view is the opposite: inputs anchored high or rising, which is WHY producers are raising prices. Both can be literally true - down slightly month-on-month, still high in level - but my framing was one-sided. THE DECISIVE EVIDENCE IS BEHAVIOURAL: mills raising prices five times in seven months is not what an industry does when its input costs are easing. SCRAP IS A THIRD INPUT THIS FILE NEVER TRACKED. The spread bridge models ore and coking coal only. Vietnamese sources name scrap alongside them as a driver of the increases. THE PART THAT MATTERS MOST, AND THE BRIDGE CANNOT SEE IT: THE REVENUE BLADE IS SPLITTING. Domestic HRC prices were reported FALLING on 13-Jul under import competition, while REBAR prices are being RAISED. HRC down, rebar up, at the same time. hpg-spread-bridge.md section 5 already lists this as its first honest limit - 'Product mix is ignored - HPG sells rebar as well as HRC, with different economics' - and that limit is now BINDING rather than theoretical. A bridge calibrated on a single HRC blade cannot represent a quarter where the two products move in opposite directions. NOTHING CHANGED. No branch, probability or weight. This is T5 and charter s2 forbids moving probs or exit_pe on T4-T6. It is recorded because H2 spread is the live variable on 16.8% of the book and because the direction of the revenue blade is now genuinely ambiguous rather than simply negative. Corroborating levels, both already consistent with this file: domestic HRC 14,000-14,350 VND/kg; iron ore ~98.02 USD/dmtu on 08-Jul against the 98.25 logged yesterday.
actuals._US_REBAR_FINAL_RATES_2026_07_30: THE FINAL RATES ARE PUBLISHED. Federal Register 2026-15438 (AD, Final Affirmative Determination of Sales at Less Than Fair Value) and 2026-15437 (CVD, Final Affirmative Countervailing Duty Determination), both dated 30-JUL-2026, applicable 30-Jul. Period of investigation 01-Oct-2024 to 31-Mar-2025. Tier T1 for the existence and dates; the RATES below are T5, from trade press, because federalregister.gov returns proxy 403 from this environment and the documents themselves could not be read. THE NUMBERS: FINAL DUMPING MARGINS FOR VIETNAM 128.53% TO 136.57%, with CASH DEPOSIT RATES ADJUSTED TO 123.49% TO 131.53% after offsetting export subsidies. Preliminary was 121.97% (Hoa Phat, mandatory respondent) to 130.77% (all others). SO THE FINALS CAME IN ABOUT 6.6pp HIGHER AT BOTH ENDS. WHICH END IS HOA PHAT IS NOT CONFIRMED, AND I AM NOT ASSERTING IT. The preliminary structure put the mandatory respondent at the LOWER rate, so 128.53% is the likely Hoa Phat figure and 136.57% the all-others - but that is an inference from structure, not a reading of the table. This is precisely the conflation warned about in _US_REBAR_IS_TWO_DUTIES_NOT_ONE_2026_07_29, and the warning applies to my own inference as much as to the press. USEFUL MECHANIC WORTH RECORDING: the CASH DEPOSIT RATE IS ~5pp BELOW THE MARGIN because of an export-subsidy offset between the AD and CVD cases. The deposit is what importers actually post, so it is the operative number for trade economics, not the headline margin. WHAT IT DOES TO THE THESIS: NOTHING, AND THAT IS THE POINT. Provisional duties near 122% have been collected since March under the extension HPG itself requested. HPG has already traded a full quarter under them, and that quarter - Q2/2026, filed 29-Jul - printed revenue +53% and NPAT +51%. Moving a prohibitive duty from ~122% to ~129% changes nothing commercially: the trade was already uneconomic and the earnings effect is already inside the reported run-rate. US is ~3% of revenue. No branch, probability, weight or confidence changed.
actuals._REBAR_IS_NOT_OVER_2026_07_31: CORRECTION TO A STATUS I RECORDED YESTERDAY. The date-gate row was marked 'RESOLVED 30-Jul' after Commerce published its final AD and CVD determinations. COMMERCE'S PART IS RESOLVED. THE CASE IS NOT. WHAT REMAINS: the US INTERNATIONAL TRADE COMMISSION must make its FINAL INJURY DETERMINATION WITHIN 45 DAYS of Commerce's finals, so a vote around MID-SEPTEMBER 2026. ONLY AFTER AN AFFIRMATIVE ITC VOTE DO THE ORDERS ACTUALLY ISSUE. If the ITC finds no material injury, no duties are imposed at all and cash deposits collected under the provisional measures are REFUNDED. WHY THIS IS WORTH RECORDING RATHER THAN FILING AWAY: THE REMAINING UNCERTAINTY ON REBAR IS NOW ASYMMETRIC TO THE UPSIDE, and nothing in this file models it. The DOWNSIDE - duties imposed at ~129% - is already inside the reported run-rate, because provisional duties near 122% have been collected since March and HPG's Q2 printed revenue +53% and NPAT +51% under them. The UPSIDE - an ITC negative, orders never issuing, deposits refunded - is not in any branch. ITC negatives in steel cases are uncommon but they are not unheard of, and the petition covers four countries so a split outcome by country is possible. NOT ADDING A BRANCH OR MOVING A PROBABILITY - both are judgment changes reserved for a human under charter s2. Recorded as a DATED CATALYST that belongs on the calendar, which is charter s1 test 3. FORECAST #10'S SCORE IS UNAFFECTED. It named the Commerce final explicitly ('~Jul 28 Federal Register') and that is what resolved it. The ITC vote is a separate event and does not reopen a scored forecast.
actuals._A_THIRD_FIGURE_FOR_THE_DIVESTMENT_GAIN_: OPEN-DECISIONS ITEM 13 MOVED FURTHER FROM RESOLUTION, NOT CLOSER, AND THAT IS WORTH SAYING PLAINLY. A THIRD CANDIDATE FIGURE APPEARED THIS SWEEP: press states that in Q1/2026 APPROXIMATELY 3,800bn came from the capital-transfer at the PHO NOI urban project. Tier T5, and explicitly approximate ('khoang'). THERE ARE NOW THREE NUMBERS FOR ONE LINE: 4,123 as carried in q1_divestment_gain; 4,010 as implied by q1_npat 9,056 minus q1_core_npat 5,046; and ~3,800 from this sweep. 3,800 is 7.8% below the file's figure and 5.2% below the implied one - TOO FAR TO BE A ROUNDING OF EITHER. IT WEAKENS THE EXPLANATION THIS FILE PREFERRED. The existing note offers 'likely explanation: 4,123 is PRE-tax and 4,010 is post-tax, implying 113bn of tax = a 2.7% effective rate, well below the 20% CIT - possible but not obvious'. A COMPETING READING NOW HAS SUPPORT: that ~3,800 IS PHO NOI ALONE while 4,123 is TOTAL divestment or other income including roughly 300bn of something else. On that reading the 113bn gap is COMPOSITION, not tax, and the tax story is unnecessary. THE FILE'S OWN H1 NON-STEEL RECONCILIATION assumed the whole 4,123 was Pho Noi ('Pho Noi one-off 4,123 + agriculture ~648 = 4,771'), so that reconciliation inherits the same ambiguity. NEITHER READING IS ESTABLISHED AND NEITHER IS ADOPTED. WHAT IT COSTS, QUANTIFIED. q1_core_npat / q1_volume_mt is the CALIBRATION ANCHOR of the spread bridge - conversion_usd_t 114 was solved backwards to reproduce it. The three candidates give: gain 4,123 -> core 4,933 -> anchor 1.644m/t; gain 4,010 -> core 5,046 -> anchor 1.682m/t; gain 3,800 -> core 5,256 -> anchor 1.752m/t. THE ANCHOR RANGE IS 1.644 TO 1.752m/t, A 6.5% SPREAD, and the new figure moves it in the OPPOSITE DIRECTION from the alternative previously considered - the file had only ever contemplated the anchor being LOWER than 1.68, and 3,800 makes it HIGHER. The bridge's whole cost structure is calibrated off this one number. A CHECK THAT DOES PASS, recorded so it is not re-litigated: 4,123 is a Q1 figure, not an H1 one. Q1 9,056 + Q2 6,424 = 15,480 = stated H1 exactly, so the quarters are clean and the gain sits inside Q1. NOTHING CHANGED. q1_divestment_gain is NOT edited - three candidate values is a reason to escalate, not to pick. The resolving document is HPG's Q1 or H1 financial statement note on other income, which this environment cannot reach.

spread_bridge_2026_07_26._FX_IS_UNLABELLED_2026_07_28: The bridge carries FX 26,300 described only as 'VND/USD market rate'. On 28-Jul there are two very different market rates: the SBV CENTRAL rate at 25,306 - an all-time high, passing the 25,298 set 25-Aug-2025 - and the FREE MARKET at 26,400-26,420. A 4.4% gap. The 26,300 in file sits 0.4% below the free market and 3.9% above the central rate, so it appears to be a free-market figure, but nothing says so. HOW MUCH THIS MATTERS DEPENDS ON SOMETHING THE BRIDGE ALSO DOES NOT STATE: whether HPG's realised HRC price is treated as USD-linked or VND-fixed. If USD-LINKED, FX multiplies a USD margin of (539 - 522) and largely CANCELS - the choice between the two rates is worth about VND 0.019m/t, trivial. If VND-FIXED, FX hits only the USD cost side and the choice is worth VND 0.576m/t - 85 to 96% of the 0.60-0.68m/t spot margin and 46% of the 1.25m bear branch. REALITY IS IN BETWEEN: roughly 80% of HRC volume is domestic and priced in VND, tracking import parity with a lag and imperfectly - and the Formosa price cut suggests domestic prices are currently set by competition rather than by FX. So partial pass-through. But the bridge does not say, which means it cannot be interrogated on the question, and that is the defect. NOT CHANGED. No branch moves and nothing here is an escalation. Recorded because it is the same species as the day's other findings - an input whose LABEL decides the answer - and it sits on the live variable days before HPG reports. A human states the pass-through assumption and names which rate applies to HPG's import settlement.
spread_bridge_2026_07_26._FX_RATE_PINNED_2026_07_29: ANSWERS the open question in _FX_IS_UNLABELLED_2026_07_28, which asked which of several 'market rates' applies to HPG's imports. It is the COMMERCIAL BANK SELL rate - what an importer actually pays to buy USD. On 28-Jul: Vietcombank 26,115/26,525 and Techcombank 26,135/26,530 (buy/sell). Not the central rate of 25,306, which is a reference; not quite the free market at ~26,410. SO THE AMBIGUITY SHRINKS FROM 4.4% TO 0.87%. The bridge uses 26,300, which is 0.87% below the bank sell rate. On 522/t of USD-priced input that understates VND cost by about 0.12m/t - roughly 18-20% of the 0.60-0.68m/t spot margin. Yesterday's worst case was 0.576m/t, so pinning the rate cuts the open question to about a fifth of what it looked like. Still not nothing on a margin this thin. SECOND FACT, and it is a constraint rather than a price: the SBV band is +/-5% around the central rate, so floor 24,041 and ceiling 26,571. Techcombank's sell rate of 26,530 sits 41 dong below that ceiling - 0.16%. With the central rate at an all-time high, commercial rates are pinned against the cap. FURTHER DONG WEAKNESS HAS TO COME THROUGH THE CENTRAL RATE, not through the market, because there is no room left in the band. That makes SBV's daily central-rate fixing the thing to watch for HPG's input costs, not the commercial quote. NOT APPLIED - the bridge's 26,300 is left as it stands. Updating it is a 0.12m/t change to a model whose pass-through assumption is still unstated (see the 28-Jul note), and doing one without the other would be false precision.
spread_bridge_2026_07_26._ANCHOR_IS_CONTAMINATED_BY_NON_STEEL_202: THIRD problem found with the 1.682m/t calibration anchor, and this one has a clear direction. Hoa Phat AGRICULTURE (HPA) filed H1/2026 today: revenue 3,379bn, NPAT 648bn, 64% of its full-year plan, implying an FY plan near 1,012bn. HPG Group itself is still unfiled. WHY IT MATTERS HERE: this bridge models HPG as a STEEL business - NPAT per tonne times tonnes - and its conversion_usd_t of 114 was SOLVED BACKWARDS so the bridge reproduces a Q1 core anchor of 1.682m/t (5,046bn over 3.0mt). But that 5,046bn is GROUP profit and includes non-steel earnings. SIZING WITH AGRICULTURE ALONE: HPA runs about 324bn a quarter, so (5,046 - 324) / 3.0mt = 1.574m/t - 6.4% below the anchor. And agriculture is only one non-steel segment; real estate, appliances, pipe and galvanised sheet also sit outside the 3.0mt basket, so a true steel-only margin is lower still. DIRECTION OF THE ERROR: an anchor that is too HIGH means the solved conversion cost is too LOW, so the bridge UNDERSTATES steel costs and OVERSTATES the spread at every price point. That is the same direction as the other two anchor problems - the 113bn core/one-off reconciliation gap (_RECONCILIATION_FLAG_2026_07_28) and the FX rate sitting 0.87% below the bank sell rate (_FX_RATE_PINNED_2026_07_29). Three separate issues, all pushing the modelled spread the same way: too generous. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: HPA's ownership percentage, so how much of the 648bn is attributable to HPG shareholders is unknown; and whether HPA's profit is inside the 5,046bn 'core' figure at all, which depends on how that core number was constructed. Both read off the segment note in the group statement. NOT APPLIED. Re-solving the conversion cost on an inferred non-steel share would replace one unverified anchor with another. The group statement lands within a day and carries the segment note that settles it.

model._HPG_OWN_AUGUST_PRICE_LANDS_ON_THE_MODEL: HOA PHAT'S OWN AUGUST HRC OFFER, which is a better instrument for this model than any third-party benchmark it has used so far. SAE1006/SS400 for August delivery: 546/t CFR north and central Vietnam, 547/t CFR south, and 535/t CFR HCMC as a NET VOLUME PRICE for orders of 20,000t or more. That is 34/t BELOW the July offer, so July was approximately 580/t. Formosa Ha Tinh followed with a ~40/t cut across August-September. Reasons given: weak rainy-season domestic demand, a REDUCED EU EXPORT QUOTA for Vietnamese steel, and slower Brazilian buying. Two independent outlets, tier T5. THE FINDING CUTS AGAINST THE CASE I HAVE BEEN BUILDING FOR THREE DAYS. This file has accumulated 'bear evidence' on the spread since 26-Jul - Formosa's cut, Indian landed at 535, ore to 115, coal to 220. The natural reading of a 34/t cut is more of the same. IT IS NOT. The bridge prices spot HRC at 539. HPG's post-cut list is 546-547 (+1.4% ABOVE the model) and its volume price is 535 (-0.7% BELOW it). THE MODEL'S SPOT INPUT SITS ALMOST EXACTLY BETWEEN HOA PHAT'S OWN LIST AND VOLUME PRICES - it is the best-calibrated input in the bridge, and the August cut is ALREADY INSIDE IT rather than a further leg down from it. Stated plainly because the opposite claim was the easy one to write: this datapoint CONFIRMS the spot case, it does not worsen it. WHAT IT DOES CHANGE IS THE SHAPE OF Q3. On the bridge's own sensitivity, each 20/t of HRC is 0.42m/t of NPAT, so the 34/t step from July to August is worth about 0.71m/t - large against branches of bear 1.25, base 1.60, bull 1.85 and a Q1 actual of 1.68. But Q3 STRADDLES THE STEP: July at ~580, August at ~546, September unknown. A quarter averaging those is ABOVE the 539 spot case, which means the proposed 'spot_persists' branch (OPEN-DECISIONS item 6) describes Q4 better than it describes Q3. Anyone reading a soft Q3 print as vindication of the spot case would be crediting it a quarter early. AND IT MAKES A KNOWN LIMITATION LIVE. circular_29_2026_tt_nhnn.note: THE FIRST REGULATION THIS REPO HAS FOUND BEFORE ITS EFFECTIVE DATE RATHER THAN AFTER, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF THE ENTRY. Circular 29/2026/TT-NHNN was ISSUED 30-JUN-2026 and takes effect 15-AUG-2026 - TWO WEEKS FROM NOW. Compare the four found in the past three days: Circular 25/2026 (four weeks late), HCMC Decision 45/2026 (one month), Circular 08/2026 (THREE months), and the credit-quota exemptions (undated). ALL FOUR WERE FOUND ONLY AFTER SOMETHING ELSE MADE THEM RELEVANT. THE BACK-SWEEP COMMITTED ONE HOUR AGO WAS RUN IMMEDIATELY AND THIS IS ITS FIRST RESULT. The lesson written at 06:53 was 'SBV and MoF circulars get a monthly back-sweep of the preceding quarter, not a search when a thesis needs one'. Running it once turned a pattern of retrospective discovery into a dated catalyst with two weeks of warning. That is the difference between writing a lesson and applying it, and it is recorded because the previous four show what the alternative costs. WHAT IT CHANGES, AS FAR AS IS ESTABLISHED. Three named areas: DEBT-HANDLING PROCEDURES, SMALL-VALUE LOAN LIMITS, and THE LEGAL FRAMEWORK FOR ELECTRONIC LENDING. Small-value loans are now quantified, at not more than 200,000,000 VND for people's credit funds - a threshold that does not touch our banks directly. Agreements signed before 15-Aug run on under the old rules, but ANY AMENDMENT after that date must comply with the new ones, so the transition reaches existing books through restructurings. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, AND IS NOT GUESSED. The amendments are known by ARTICLE NUMBER (Art.1 cl.3, Art.2 cl.13, Art.8 cl.6(b), Art.18 cl.4, Art.22 cl.2(h)) and by press characterisation, NOT by text - thuvienphapluat's full-text page returns proxy 403, the SIXTH host to refuse this session. Article 8 of Circular 39 is the list of purposes credit institutions may NOT lend for, so an amendment there is potentially the most consequential of the five, BUT THIS FILE HAS NOT READ IT and will not infer its content from its location. One outlet headlines the circular as good news for borrowers; whether that is neutral, positive or negative for LENDER margins is a different question and is unanswered. WHY IT PLAUSIBLY MATTERS HERE, STATED AS A REASON TO WATCH RATHER THAN A FINDING: the three areas are retail and consumer lending, and this book holds VPB (which contains FE CREDIT), MBB (which contains MCREDIT) and TCB, 51.5% between them. The electronic-lending framework is the piece most likely to matter to a digital-first lender. NOTHING MODELLED, no confidence moved, no branch touched.

The 31-Jul lesson that EFFECTIVE DATES CLUSTER - written after 01-Jul turned out to carry both Circular 25/2026 and HCMC Decision 45/2026 - now has a second instance, and this time the cluster is FOURTEEN DAYS AHEAD rather than a month behind. The circular governs 'cong ty tai chinh TONG HOP' (GENERAL finance companies) and 'cong ty cho thue tai chinh' (FINANCIAL LEASING companies). This book reaches two finance companies through its banks: FE CREDIT (VPB) and MCREDIT (MBB). Both appear to be CONSUMER finance companies rather than general or leasing ones - MCredit's legal name is 'Cong ty Tai chinh TIN DUNG TIEU DUNG TNHH MB Shinsei', consumer credit written into the name itself, and FE Credit is 'Cong ty Tai chinh TNHH MTV Ngan hang Viet Nam Thinh Vuong', whose business descends directly from VPBank's consumer credit division. Vietnam's Law on Credit Institutions separates GENERAL finance companies from SPECIALISED ones, and consumer finance is a specialised type that does not conduct financial leasing. HEDGED DELIBERATELY: THIS IS READ FROM COMPANY NAMES AND PRESS DESCRIPTIONS, NOT FROM THE LICENCES. A licence is the only thing that settles which category a company holds, and this environment cannot reach the SBV register. The finding is 'probably out of scope', not 'out of scope'. RECORDED AS A NEGATIVE RESULT SO IT IS NOT RE-RAISED. A regulation that LOOKED like it touched two holdings' subsidiaries was checked and probably does not. _regulatory._THE_THREE_BANK_STOCK_ISSUES_ARE_NOT_THE: THE SET IS COMPLETE AND THE ANSWER IS COUNTERINTUITIVE. After pinning VPB's label an hour ago, the same check was run on the other two flags written in the same form - the 29-Jul lesson that when one stale flag is found, every other flag of the same shape gets checked in the same sweep. ALL THREE ARE NOW PINNED AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME INSTRUMENT. TCB 60%, over 4.28bn shares, charter capital +42,876bn: BONUS SHARES ISSUED FROM OWNER'S EQUITY (co phieu thuong). A capital restructuring, NOT a dividend distribution. Separately its 7% cash (4,960bn) IS from undistributed profit and is a real dividend. VPB 26.04%, 2.06bn shares: STOCK DIVIDEND FROM RETAINED EARNINGS, amended in July from an owner's-equity bonus issue approved at the 22-Apr AGM. MBB 15%, over 1.2bn shares, 12,082bn: STOCK DIVIDEND FROM UNDISTRIBUTED ACCUMULATED PROFIT of 21,234bn at 31-Dec-2025, part of a 25% total distribution worth 20,137bn of which 8,055bn is the 10% cash. SO THE LARGEST OF THE THREE STOCK ISSUES IS THE ONE THAT IS NOT A TAXABLE DISTRIBUTION, AND THE TWO SMALLER ONES ARE. That is the opposite of what 'TCB is paying 67%' suggests, and it is exactly the distinction that disappears when all three are recorded as 'a big stock issue pending'. SIZED ON THE FILE'S OWN TAX_DIVIDEND = 0.05, par basis, at on-file prices: TCB 0.12% of price (cash only), VPB 0.62%, MBB 0.57%. Weighted by position that is 0.042 / 0.062 / 0.037pp, TOTALLING 0.141pp OF THE WHOLE BOOK from three names that are 51.5% of it. THREE CAVEATS, STATED BECAUSE THE NUMBER LOOKS MORE SOLID THAN IT IS. (1) Vietnamese PIT on stock dividends is generally COLLECTED ON DISPOSAL, not at issuance, so this is a DEFERRED liability rather than a current cost - it reduces realised proceeds whenever the holder sells, which for a long-term holder may be years away. (2) The 5% rate is the file's own assumption in cfa.py and has NOT been verified against current law this sweep; the draft MoF decree carried as TAX_GAINS_DRAFT = 0.20 shows the regime is in flux. (3) Prices are the undated ones OPEN-DECISIONS item 2 already flags. WHAT IT ADDS TO ITEM 3: that item asks a human to set a cash_yield convention. The answer now needs THREE cells, not one - cash dividend, stock dividend, and bonus issue - because the book holds one of each and they are taxed differently. Recording all three as 'pending corporate action' was hiding a real difference between the two largest positions.

circular_121_2020_tt_btc.subject: Total margin lending by a securities company must not exceed 200% of OWNER'S EQUITY
circular_121_2020_tt_btc.also: Quyet dinh 87/QD-UBCK (2017) governs the margin trading regime; per-stock loan ratios run 10-50% by ticker
circular_121_2020_tt_btc.tier: T1/T2 instrument, named from T5 sources
circular_121_2020_tt_btc.note: THE RULE THE FILE HAS BEEN USING WITHOUT NAMING, PLUS THE NUMBER IT NEVER COMPUTED. This repo already applies a 2.0x cap - VCI's note reads 'margin 16,644 / 0.97 = equity 17,159' against 'a 2.0x cap', and VPX's derives 'ceiling >=71,177 => equity >=35,588' from it. NEITHER NAMED THE INSTRUMENT. It is CIRCULAR 121/2020/TT-BTC: total margin debt of a securities company may not exceed 200% OF OWNER'S EQUITY. Per-stock lending ratios run 10-50% depending on the ticker, under Decision 87/QD-UBCK (2017). 'Margin rules 91/102' is named in the lane definition and returns ZERO hits in this repo; the binding instrument is 121/2020, so the lane text may be pointing at the wrong circulars. AND HERE IS WHAT WAS NEVER COMPUTED: TCBS'S OWN UTILISATION. On this file's figures - TCX market cap pe_ttm 20.3 x npat_ttm 4,050 = 82,215bn, at P/B 2.49 - implied EQUITY is ~33,018bn, so the regulatory ceiling is ~66,036bn. TCBS'S MARGIN BOOK OF 51,500bn IS THEREFORE ~1.56x EQUITY, OR 78% OF THE REGULATORY CAP, with headroom of roughly 14,500bn. THE THREE BROKERS SIT AT VERY DIFFERENT UTILISATIONS AND THE FILE HAD ONLY LOOKED AT TWO: VCI 0.97x, VPX ~1.07x, TCBS ~1.56x. THE FILE HAS CRITICISED VCI FOR NOT USING ITS CAPACITY - 'unused capacity that stays unused in the best conditions on record is a description of the business, not an option on it' - and has treated VPX's >33,000bn of unused room as its REAL BULL CASE, better than the CAEX option. IT NEVER NOTICED THAT TCX IS THE ONE ACTUALLY LEVERED. WHICH REFRAMES THE TCX CASE WITHOUT CONTRADICTING IT. TCX ranks first on expected return and earns ~31% of H1 PBT from margin interest on that 51,500bn book. Those earnings come from a balance sheet that is MORE THAN THREE QUARTERS DRAWN AGAINST ITS REGULATORY LIMIT, so the margin line cannot grow much faster than equity does. The same fact that makes VCI look inert makes TCX look constrained - and neither reading was available while only two of the three were measured. NOTE WHAT DOES NOT RELIEVE IT: TCB's 60% BONUS ISSUE MOVES RESERVES INTO CHARTER CAPITAL AND DOES NOT INCREASE TOTAL OWNER'S EQUITY - and in any case it is the PARENT's equity, not TCBS's. Capacity at TCBS moves on retained earnings or a capital injection, neither of which is on file. STATED WITH ITS CAVEAT: TCX's equity here is DERIVED from pe_ttm x npat_ttm / P/B, not read from a balance sheet, and npat_ttm cross-checks have already failed twice in this repo (VCI 25.2% off, VPX 9-27% off). SO 1.56x IS AN ESTIMATE BUILT ON FILE FIGURES, NOT A FILED NUMBER. It is directionally robust - TCBS would need equity above 25,750bn merely to be legal at 51,500bn - but the precise utilisation needs TCBS's reported equity. ESCALATED, NOT MODELLED.

_peer_reads._BANK_Q2_PEERS_POINT_DOWN_2026_07_29: PEER PRINTS LANDED AND THEY GO THE OTHER WAY FROM CONSENSUS, one day before MBB files and calibration forecast #4 resolves. ACB Q2/2026: NPAT 4,292bn, DOWN 12.06% YoY; PBT 5,366bn, down 12%. But NET INTEREST INCOME was 7,784bn, UP 16.5% YoY, and customer loans grew 8.6% to 745,759bn. THE ENTIRE MISS IS PROVISIONING - ACB sharply increased credit-risk provisions. VIB Q2 profit 1,905.42bn, DOWN 8.24%. Saigonbank posted a LOSS; VietABank down double digits. Sector-level: Q2 NPAT for covered banks forecast +15% YoY and H1 +16%, but PROVISIONING EXPENSE forecast +19% YoY on existing NPL pressure. WHY THIS MATTERS TOMORROW. MBB's Q2 PBT estimate on file is 8,812bn, +18% YoY. ACB printed -12% and VIB -8.24%. The peers with actual numbers are running well below what the sector forecast implies, and the mechanism is specific and testable: TOP LINE IS FINE, CREDIT COST IS THE SWING. MBB's Q1 NPL was 1.42%. If the same pattern holds, the 8,812bn estimate is optimistic. NOT A FORECAST CHANGE AND NOT A CONFIDENCE CHANGE. This is information about ACB and VIB, not about MBB, and charter s2 does not permit peer results to move a held name's confidence. It is recorded because calibration forecast #4 resolves within 24 hours and this is the best available leading indicator - registering it now means the read is not constructed after the print. AND IT QUALIFIES THIS AFTERNOON'S TT25 CONCLUSION. At 17:53 Circular 25/2026 was logged as easing the FUNDING constraint on credit growth, which it does. These prints say the constraint actually binding on bank PROFIT right now is CREDIT COST, not funding. Both can be true - more room to lend does not make the lending safer - but the TT25 note read as unambiguously supportive and it should not have. More capacity to grow into a rising provisioning cycle is not the same as more profit. Recorded as a correction of emphasis, not of fact.
_peer_reads._VIB_PROVISIONING_DOUBLED_AND_MBB_STILL_: SHARPENS THIS MORNING'S READ-ACROSS FINDING RATHER THAN OVERTURNING IT. VIB's Q2/2026 credit-risk provisioning ROSE 101.6% to 1,280bn - more than doubled - against PBT -8.24%. So the sector provisioning cycle inferred from ACB and VIB WAS REAL AT THOSE BANKS; the mechanism existed and was correctly identified. WHAT FAILED WAS THE TRANSMISSION, not the observation: MBB printed Q2 PBT +40% with net interest income +36.55% and NPL coverage RISING to 93.63% in the same quarter. Also filed this week: BaoViet Bank Q2 profit -50% on provisioning, and VietABank Q2 provisioning up ~19x off a tiny base. THE CORRECTED LESSON IS NARROWER AND MORE USEFUL than 'peer read-across is unreliable'. Several Vietnamese banks did provision heavily in Q2/2026. MBB did not visibly join them. A read-across is a claim that a shared driver reaches a specific book, and the banks it reached (ACB, VIB, BaoViet, VietABank) versus the one it did not (MBB) is itself the question worth asking - MBB's own Q1 provisioning was +15.7% against PBT +14.8%, which was the bank-specific evidence that contradicted the inference and was correctly acted on before the print. STILL UNKNOWN AND STILL THE GAP: MBB's H1 provisioning figure. A second search this sweep again returned only the Q1 number (3,454.8bn, +15.7%), explicitly labelled Q1 - which independently re-confirms this morning's call that the figure circulating in Q2-context coverage was the Q1 one.
_peer_reads._VPS_IPO_TERMS_ARE_A_LIVE_COMPARABLE_FOR: VPS APPEARS IN THIS FILE AS A COMPETITOR AND ITS IPO TERMS DO NOT. Now recorded: ticker VCK, listing sought on HOSE, minimum offer price 60,000/share for up to 202.31m shares, implying a valuation of about US$3.4bn and charter capital rising above 16,400bn. Book-built through VPS plus SSI, MBS, FPTS, KIS, SHS, DNSE and OCBS. The minimum price was RAISED from 22,457 to 60,000 - a 2.67x increase in the ask. Tier T5. WHY IT TOUCHES A HOLDING. The TCX case in this file rests on an explicit statement that THE RISK IS THE MULTIPLE, NOT THE EARNINGS - 2.49x P/B, the priciest in the book. There is currently no fresh public comparable for a large Vietnamese broker. A VPS LISTING WOULD CREATE ONE. At FX 26,300, US$3.4bn is ~89,420bn, which is ABOUT 9% ABOVE TCX'S IMPLIED MARKET CAP OF ~82,215bn (pe_ttm 20.3 x npat_ttm 4,050) - and VPS's margin book is 31,300bn against TCBS's 51,500bn, so VPS is asking to be valued ABOVE TCX ON A MARGIN BOOK 39% SMALLER. Different mix (VPS leads RETAIL BROKERAGE share, TCBS leads MARGIN), so this is a comparable to watch, not an arbitrage. P/B DELIBERATELY NOT COMPUTED. Charter capital is PAR VALUE, not equity, and at 60,000 on 10,000 par most of the ~12,139bn raised would be share premium, so post-money equity is well above 16,400bn by an amount this file does not know. Computing a P/B from charter capital would be exactly the measure error charter s3 check 3 exists to stop. AND THE TERMS MAY BE STALE - THIS IS THE PART THAT NEEDS SAYING. The 60,000 minimum was announced in OCTOBER 2025 for an offering window of Q4/2025 to Q1/2026. THAT WINDOW HAS PASSED. As recently as JUNE 2026 a VPS executive was on the record that choosing a valuation 'that satisfies all parties is not easy', which is a public admission that pricing was still contested eight months after the number was published. So the terms are recorded as ANNOUNCED, with the slippage flagged, not as current market truth. WHAT TO WATCH IS THE DIRECTION IT EVENTUALLY PRINTS: a successful listing near US$3.4bn supports TCX's multiple; a repricing down, or further slippage, is a negative read on the whole cluster - which is 19.5% of this book on a look-through basis, not the 11.4% stated. Nothing modelled, no confidence moved (T5, charter s2).
_peer_reads._A_PEER_FOUNDING_FAMILY_BOUGHT_IN_THE_SA: A CHECK ON WHETHER KDH'S INSIDER BUY IS NAME-SPECIFIC, RUN BECAUSE THE MBB READ-ACROSS FAILURE ARGUES FOR RUNNING IT IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. NAM LONG (NLG), an HCMC residential developer on the lane-6 competitor list, disclosed that NGUYEN NAM and NGUYEN HIEP - TWO SONS OF CHAIRMAN NGUYEN XUAN QUANG - EACH BOUGHT 1 MILLION NLG SHARES BETWEEN 8 AND 30 JULY 2026, by negotiated and matched orders. Tier T5. WHY IT QUALIFIES A SIGNAL ALREADY ON FILE. _INSIDER_BUY_DETAIL_2026_07_29 reads KDH's registration as 'founding-family accumulation routed through a recently appointed executive' and notes that a family buying its own shares after a fall is more often a positive signal than a negative one. THAT READING TREATS THE BUY AS INFORMATION ABOUT KDH. If a peer's founding family is doing the same thing in the same weeks, part of the signal may be about HCMC RESIDENTIAL PROPERTY OR ABOUT PRICE WEAKNESS rather than about KDH - the VN-Index fell to 1,686 on 24-Jul from a Q2 peak above 1,927, which is a reason for any founder to buy. STATED PROPORTIONATELY, AND THE SCALE DIFFERENCE IS LARGE. NLG: 2m shares total across two buyers, COMPLETED 8-30 JUL. KDH: 20m shares by one buyer, taking him from 0.056% to 1.838% - a THIRTY-THREE-FOLD stake increase - REGISTERED 20-Jul with the window still open to 21-AUG. Two completed 1m purchases and one 20m registration are not the same event, and this does NOT overturn the KDH reading. It bounds it: the KDH buy is no longer the only founding-family purchase in HCMC residential this July, so its name-specific content is smaller than a single-name reading implies. THE METHOD POINT IS THE DURABLE PART. On 31-Jul a peer read-across FAILED - ACB -12% and VIB -8% did not predict MBB's +40% - and the lesson drawn was that a read-across must name the mechanism reaching the specific book. THE MIRROR OBLIGATION IS THIS ONE: before treating a signal as NAME-SPECIFIC, check whether peers show it too. Both errors are the same failure to ask what is shared and what is not. ALSO NOTED, NOT A HOLDING: SSI goes ex on 17-AUG for a 10% cash dividend plus a 5:1 capital increase, issuing over 500.2m new shares, cash paid from 14-Sep. Cluster context for the brokers only. NOTHING MODELLED, no confidence moved.
